sources.title: AI features and your website
sources.notes: Supports ordinary search eligibility and snippet requirements for AI features. No extra AI markup is required; inclusion is not guaranteed. For dedicated owner-side generative-AI reporting, use the separate google-generative-ai-report reference and native measurement rule.

sources.title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
sources.notes: Supports original value and transparent authorship and production methods. ARWP editorial workflows are implementation proposals, not a disclosed ranking formula.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search
sources.notes: Supports rejecting scaled low-value content, doorway pages, link spam, cloaking, and deceptive practices; applies to generative search responses too.

sources.title: Introduction to robots.txt
sources.notes: Crawl management does not equal guaranteed deindexing or access control.

sources.title: Robots meta tags and HTTP header specifications
sources.notes: Supports noindex and snippet controls. Crawlers must access a page to observe page-level directives.

sources.title: Specify a canonical URL
sources.notes: Canonical signals consolidate duplicates; the publisher preference is not proof of the search engine-selected canonical.

sources.title: Build and submit a sitemap
sources.notes: Supports canonical URL lists and meaningful lastmod. Submission is a discovery hint, not indexing evidence.

sources.title: JavaScript SEO basics
sources.notes: Supports inspecting rendering, links, status handling, and indexable content; server HTML is an ARWP interoperability choice rather than a universal Google requirement.

sources.title: Google Search technical requirements
sources.notes: Supports crawl access, successful status, and indexable content as eligibility requirements; does not promise serving.

sources.title: General structured data guidelines
sources.notes: Markup must represent visible, relevant content and use supported properties. Syntax or Rich Results Test success cannot prove truthful claims or rich-result appearance.

sources.title: Article structured data
sources.notes: Supports article author, date, headline, and image properties where accurate; no authorship credential is created by markup.

sources.title: Dataset structured data
sources.notes: Describes dataset discovery metadata including provenance and distribution. Dataset eligibility is not ordinary search ranking or verified data quality.

sources.title: Organization structured data
sources.notes: Supports identifying real organizations and applicable properties. Do not invent registration, membership, addresses, or corporate scale.

sources.title: Breadcrumb structured data
sources.notes: Describes page hierarchy markup, not keyword paths or a guaranteed search presentation.

sources.title: Introduction to Product structured data
sources.notes: Separates product snippets and merchant listings; select the applicable feature guide and satisfy its current requirements.

sources.title: Local business structured data
sources.notes: Supports accurate location-specific business information. An online-only service must not invent a physical location.

sources.title: Write high-quality reviews
sources.notes: Supports first-hand evidence, relevant quantitative criteria, trade-offs, and comparisons. ARWP scorecards and experiment designs remain publisher proposals.

sources.title: Influencing title links
sources.notes: Supports descriptive distinctive titles and consistency with visible headings. Google may generate a different title link.

sources.title: Control snippets in search results
sources.notes: Supports page-specific descriptions and preview controls; supplied descriptions are not guaranteed to be displayed.

sources.title: Link best practices
sources.notes: Supports real href links, contextual anchors, and links to important pages. No fixed internal-link count is prescribed.

sources.title: Localized versions of pages
sources.notes: Supports reciprocal language alternate annotations and valid regional codes where variants exist.

sources.title: Managing multilingual and multi-regional sites
sources.notes: Supports distinct language URLs and explicit navigation. Translation alone is not evidence of local service availability.

sources.title: Site moves with URL changes
sources.notes: Supports explicit URL mapping, redirects, updated references, and migration monitoring; traffic fluctuations remain possible.

sources.title: Managing crawling of faceted navigation URLs
sources.notes: Current destination of the Search Central guide. Supports controlling unbounded URL combinations; not blanket deletion of useful filtered pages.

sources.title: HTTP status codes and Google crawlers
sources.notes: Current destination of the Search Central guide. Successful HTTP transport does not prove the content is useful or indexed.

sources.title: Image SEO best practices
sources.notes: Supports descriptive context, accessible images, stable delivery, and applicable image metadata; no visibility guarantee.

sources.title: Video SEO best practices
sources.notes: Supports dedicated watch pages where appropriate and stable accessible media. An indexed page does not establish video indexing.

sources.title: Understanding page experience
sources.notes: Supports useful page experience without treating a single score as a complete ranking or quality measure.

sources.title: Web Vitals
sources.notes: Supports LCP, INP, CLS and field assessment at the 75th percentile by device. Lab results must not be presented as field measurements.

sources.title: Search documentation updates
sources.notes: The FAQ rich result was discontinued starting 2026-05-07 and its documentation later removed. Useful visible FAQs can still serve readers.

sources.title: IndexNow protocol documentation
sources.notes: Supports notifying participating engines of changed URLs using key verification. Acceptance is not crawling, indexing, or ranking; do not describe it as Google submission.

sources.title: Search Console impressions, clicks, and position
sources.notes: Defines provider-specific metrics and aggregation. Average position is not a stable universal rank or an AI recommendation share.

sources.title: Search Analytics query API
sources.notes: Supports dimensions, filters, and API queries. Returned rows are not guaranteed to cover every query; privacy and service limits affect completeness.

sources.title: Debugging Search traffic drops
sources.notes: Supports segmentation and checking technical, demand, and system changes before causal conclusions.

sources.title: Ask Google to recrawl URLs
sources.notes: Supports URL Inspection requests for selected URLs and sitemaps for larger sets; repeated requests do not force earlier crawling.

sources.title: Qualify outbound links
sources.notes: Supports sponsored and ugc link relationship labels; a disclosed relationship is not an independent endorsement.

sources.title: Overview of OpenAI crawlers
sources.notes: OAI-SearchBot controls automatic search crawling; GPTBot concerns foundation-model training; ChatGPT-User serves user requests. Published IP lists support verification. Allowing access cannot promise citation.

sources.title: AI Performance in Bing Webmaster Tools
sources.notes: Describes citation counts, cited pages, sampled grounding queries, and supported Microsoft surfaces. These metrics do not indicate rank, placement, authority, or other providers.

sources.title: JSON-LD 1.1
sources.notes: Supports linked-data identifiers and graphs. JSON-LD standard conformance alone does not create search-engine recognition of a property.

sources.title: HTML custom data attributes
sources.notes: Allows application-private data-* metadata. ARWP evidence attributes are a local editorial convention, not search-engine instructions or a ranking feature.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices
sources.notes: Supports persistent identifiers, provenance, quality, versions, access, and feedback. ARWP acceptance tests are proposed implementations, not W3C SEO claims.

sources.title: Schema.org Person
sources.notes: Vocabulary for real published identity and relationships. knowsAbout suggests a topic, not proof of expertise.

sources.title: Schema.org sameAs
sources.notes: Identity-equivalent references only; a related resource or admired brand is not the same entity.

sources.title: Schema.org Service
sources.notes: Vocabulary for services, providers, and areas served; no general Service rich-result promise.

sources.title: Schema.org SoftwareApplication
sources.notes: Vocabulary for application facts. Search feature eligibility must be checked independently.

sources.title: Schema.org DefinedTerm
sources.notes: Vocabulary for a defined concept and its term set; not a special AI search feature.

sources.title: Schema.org DataDownload
sources.notes: Vocabulary for dataset download representation and media properties; a described download must actually exist.

sources.title: Schema.org Claim
sources.notes: Represents a claim. Encoding a statement does not establish truth or independent fact-checking.

sources.title: Schema.org citation
sources.notes: CreativeWork citation relationships can reference works or text. A citation alone is not evidence of agreement.

sources.title: Schema.org Dataset
sources.notes: Vocabulary including measurements, coverage, and parts. Structured metadata is not verification of scientific validity.

sources.title: Accessible tables
sources.notes: Supports accessible HTML semantics and human navigation; not evidence of a search ranking effect.

sources.title: Accessible images
sources.notes: Supports accessible HTML semantics and human navigation; not evidence of a search ranking effect.

sources.title: Page structure
sources.notes: Supports accessible HTML semantics and human navigation; not evidence of a search ranking effect.

sources.title: The cite element
sources.notes: Explains cite as the title of a referenced work; the actual clickable source belongs in an anchor.

sources.title: ETag header
sources.notes: Documents HTTP validation; observed documentation includes syntax, examples, specifications, and compatibility links. Their layout is an editorial pattern, not a proven ranking cause.

sources.title: Idempotent requests
sources.notes: Observed executable request plus failure and retry boundaries. This is product documentation evidence; borrowing the structure does not prove discoverability lift.

sources.title: API upgrades
sources.notes: Observed version-aware upgrade guidance and breaking-change handling. Do not transplant Stripe-specific product behavior.

sources.title: Workers limits
sources.notes: Observed explicit resource limits and plan distinctions. Use the disclosure pattern with your own verified numbers, never copy limits as facts about another product.

sources.title: Managing repository releases
sources.notes: Observed prerequisites, CLI/browser routes, release assets, and prerelease distinctions. Actual publication must be verified separately.

sources.title: Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console
sources.notes: Documents dedicated generative-AI impression and page reporting for Search and Discover, with worldwide rollout noted as of 2026-08-31. These observations remain included in overall performance. Authenticated property data is required; do not infer separate AI metrics from aggregate Web exports or assume API availability.

sources.title: RFC 9745: Deprecation HTTP response header
sources.notes: Defines the resource-scoped Deprecation date and deprecation documentation link; a signal does not itself change resource behavior.

sources.title: RFC 8594: Sunset HTTP header
sources.notes: Sunset signals expected resource unavailability, distinct from deprecation or cache expiry.

sources.title: Immutable releases
sources.notes: Published immutable releases protect tags and assets and have release attestations; release title and notes remain editable.

sources.title: Verify release integrity
sources.notes: Documents gh release verify and verify-asset; generated source archives cannot be checked with verify-asset.

sources.title: If-Match HTTP header
sources.notes: Strong ETag preconditions can prevent conflicting updates; stale conditions fail instead of overwriting a newer representation.

sources.title: Vary HTTP header
sources.notes: Vary names request headers affecting representation selection; use consistently, including default and 304 responses.

sources.title: HTTP range requests
sources.notes: Documents partial 206 responses, Content-Range, 416 and If-Range validation; unsupported range requests may return the entire body.

sources.title: RFC 6906: profile link relation
sources.notes: The profile relation identifies additional representation conventions without changing the underlying media-type semantics.

sources.title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
sources.notes: Defines problem type identity and structured details; clients should not parse prose detail, and implementations must avoid leaking internals.

sources.title: OpenAPI 3.2.0 Link Object
sources.notes: Design-time links map responses to operations through operationId or operationRef and runtime expressions; they do not guarantee successful invocation.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding: Label in Name
sources.notes: For text-labelled controls the accessible name includes the visible label, supporting speech activation; the Understanding document is informative.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding: Status Messages
sources.notes: Status changes are programmatically determinable for assistive technology without requiring focus to move.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding: Dragging Movements
sources.notes: Author-provided dragging has an equivalent single-pointer alternative unless essential; keyboard support is a separate requirement.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
sources.notes: Author-created content must not entirely hide the component receiving keyboard focus; this is narrower than full visibility.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices: Modal Dialog Pattern
sources.notes: Describes initial focus, contained Tab sequence, Escape dismissal and logical focus restoration for modal dialogs.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding: Redundant Entry
sources.notes: Repeated information in the same process is populated or selectable, with essential, security and validity exceptions.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
sources.notes: Credential paste and password-manager assistance can avoid memory or transcription burdens; these alone do not establish full authentication conformance.

sources.title: DCAT Version 3: Dataset series
sources.notes: DatasetSeries and inSeries describe related datasets, such as annual releases, with series metadata reflecting member coverage.

sources.title: Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data
sources.notes: Defines machine-readable column types, null tokens, required values and CSV dialect metadata.

sources.title: Croissant Format Specification 1.0
sources.notes: Describes physical FileObject/FileSet distributions, checksums and RecordSet field mappings for loading real datasets.

sources.title: FAIR Signposting Profile
sources.notes: Typed links distinguish scholarly landing pages, persistent citation identifiers, metadata and downloadable content.

sources.title: Product variant structured data
sources.notes: ProductGroup, variesBy, hasVariant and productGroupID describe genuine product variants and their selectable URLs.

sources.title: Merchant return policy structured data
sources.notes: MerchantReturnPolicy describes actual applicable countries, return windows, methods and fees; policy values must reflect the merchant offer.

sources.title: Product snippets: editorial pros and cons
sources.notes: Pros-and-cons appearance is eligible only for editorial product reviews; requires at least two visible statements, not merchant or customer reviews.

sources.title: Google Benchmark user guide: repetitions and random interleaving
sources.notes: Repeated runs report dispersion; optional random interleaving reduces sensitivity to changing system state.

sources.title: JSON Schema: Dialect and vocabulary declaration
sources.notes: Root $schema declares the dialect; externally referenced schemas need their own declarations and custom assertion keywords need supporting implementations.

sources.title: JSON Schema: Modular schema combination
sources.notes: $id sets the schema base identifier for reference resolution; an identifier is not automatically a fetchable endpoint.

sources.title: RFC 7089: Memento time-based resource access
sources.notes: TimeGate datetime negotiation and TimeMaps connect current resources with actual archived prior states.

sources.title: WAI Page Structure: Page Regions
sources.notes: Native header, footer, nav and main elements identify their page regions. Repeated navigation areas can carry labels. Informative implementation guidance; not a standalone accessibility certification.

sources.title: WAI Page Structure: Labeling Regions
sources.notes: Distinct labels identify repeated region types; unique regions do not need redundant labels. Informative implementation guidance; not a standalone accessibility certification.

sources.title: WCAG Technique G1: Skip to main content
sources.notes: A skip link moves keyboard focus to the main content and must be visible at least when focused. G1 is one sufficient technique, not the only conforming solution. Informative implementation guidance; not a standalone accessibility certification.

sources.title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search
sources.notes: Supports audience value and rejects mandatory chunking, AI-only prose and special schema. Rechecked living guide; not a newly released algorithm.

sources.title: Five new ways to explore the web with generative AI in Search
sources.notes: May 6, 2026 product announcement: deeper exploration and firsthand perspectives. Does not disclose selection weights or guarantee publisher exposure.

sources.title: Voice and tone
sources.notes: Writing guidance for developer documentation, not Search ranking guidance. Adapt tone to audience and task.

sources.title: Headings and titles
sources.notes: Task and concept heading conventions support reader navigation. Grammar and heading counts are not ranking weights.

sources.title: Optimizing your content for inclusion in AI search answers
sources.notes: October 2025 guidance on clarity and structure. Provider advice is not a cross-engine causal result; punctuation advice is not a universal rule.

sources.title: Search generative AI control
sources.notes: Inclusion, exclusion and inherited property controls; rollout note dated August 31, 2026. A public crawl cannot inspect the owner setting.

sources.title: Generative AI performance report (Search)
sources.notes: Documents impression reporting and its scope. Report availability and owner observations remain separate; no invented prompt or click dimensions.

sources.title: WebPageElement
sources.notes: Open-vocabulary page-element semantics. No documented Google citation advantage.

sources.title: hasPart
sources.notes: A CreativeWork may contain another CreativeWork. Relation does not imply independent verification or endorsement.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.notes: Text selectors target passages for participating annotation clients; not a Search submission format.

sources.title: Speakable structured data (beta)
sources.notes: Documents a bounded news voice feature with country/language restrictions; not a general AI citation selector.

sources.title: Discussion forum structured data
sources.notes: Models genuine forum discussions and comments, with feature-specific eligibility. Does not turn authored marketing copy into community experience.

sources.title: Build agent-friendly websites
sources.notes: Browser-agent interaction guidance for screenshots, HTML and accessibility trees. Runtime completion is distinct from search ranking.

sources.title: Digital Object Identifier (DOI)
sources.notes: A reserved identifier is registered upon publication; DOI metadata supports identification and interlinking, not quality certification.

sources.title: About CITATION files
sources.notes: CFF supplies reusable citation metadata and distinguishes software from preferred citations. It does not establish scholarly review.

sources.title: Dataset Cards
sources.notes: Cards describe datasets, licenses, limitations and discovery tags for the Hub. No cross-engine ranking claim.

sources.title: Review criteria
sources.notes: Research-software review criteria include scope, actual development history and community evidence. These are venue requirements, not universal website rules.

sources.title: Show HN Guidelines
sources.notes: Show HN requires a substantive personally developed artifact people can try. It is not a link-directory or routine update channel.

sources.title: Connecting to Works
sources.notes: Typed related identifiers describe specific relationships. Relations deposited by an owner do not establish independent reuse.

sources.title: Consuming Citations and References
sources.notes: Citation events can originate in deposited related identifiers; removing a relation may not remove its prior event. Review underlying evidence.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
sources.notes: ALCE separates correctness and citation quality in its evaluation. This supports measurement distinctions, not present-day platform ranking claims.

sources.title: Image metadata and licensing
sources.notes: Supports truthful image-specific metadata and scoped feature eligibility; metadata does not grant rights.

sources.title: Fix lazy-loaded website content
sources.notes: Supports loading important content without requiring user interaction and testing rendered output.

sources.title: URL structure best practices
sources.notes: Supports readable, encoded and consistent URL construction; not a mandate to migrate working URLs.

sources.title: Software app structured data
sources.notes: Feature-specific eligibility and actual offer facts; do not invent reviews to satisfy requirements.

sources.title: UnitPriceSpecification vocabulary
sources.notes: Development vocabulary page reviewed as a living document, not a pinned release or a Google feature contract.

sources.title: Forms tutorial
sources.notes: Supports accessible form labels, instructions, validation and notifications; actual delivery and conversion require separate checks.

sources.title: URL Inspection tool
sources.notes: Indexed observations and live tests have different coverage; neither guarantees appearance.

sources.title: Pagination and incremental page loading
sources.notes: Supports sequential crawlable links and distinct page URLs and canonicals.

sources.title: mainEntity
sources.notes: Defines the primary entity described by a creative work, not a ranking benefit.

sources.title: Contents of a GitHub Docs article
sources.notes: Editorial precedent for prerequisites and troubleshooting. GitHub house style is not a universal SEO requirement.

tactics.title: Return the real page state
tactics.problem: An error template can masquerade as an indexable page.
implementation: Fetch priority URLs with redirects enabled.
Return 200 for usable pages and genuine 404 or 410 for removed content.
verification: No error template returns 200 in the priority sample.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Clear HTTP states may reduce indexing confusion.
tactics.anti_pattern: Treating every 200 response as healthy content.
tactics.measurement: Track valid-content responses divided by sampled priority URLs weekly.

support.locator: HTTP status codes > 2xx (success), 3xx (redirection), 4xx (client errors)
support.note: Success responses enter further processing, including possible soft-404 treatment for error content. Removed URLs returning 404/410 are not indexed. Redirects lead to the final response.

tactics.title: Audit robots rules by crawler
tactics.problem: A wildcard block can disable intended discovery.
implementation: Fetch the deployed root robots.txt.
Evaluate priority paths for each intended crawler using that provider's current documentation; record unknown when crawler-specific behavior has not been verified.
verification: Record allow, disallow, or unknown per crawler and path, including the matching rule and provider documentation used.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Removing unintended blocks restores crawl eligibility.
tactics.anti_pattern: Using robots.txt as authentication or proof of deindexing.
tactics.measurement: Count unintentionally blocked canonical URLs before and after deployment.

support.locator: Introduction; Understand the limitations of a robots.txt file
support.note: Robots rules manage access, cannot secure content, and do not reliably remove URLs from results. Google explicitly cautions that crawler interpretations differ.

tactics.title: Check snippet eligibility before AI work
tactics.problem: Preview restrictions can conflict with the desired AI-search exposure.
implementation: Inspect robots meta tags and X-Robots-Tag headers.
Document whether priority pages should allow indexing and snippets.
verification: Each target has an explicit preview policy consistent with its live directives.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Eligible indexed pages can be considered for supporting links.
tactics.anti_pattern: Promising AI inclusion after removing nosnippet.
tactics.measurement: Track priority pages with conflicting noindex or snippet directives.

support.locator: Technical requirements for appearing in AI features
support.note: Google AI supporting links require an indexed page eligible for a Search snippet, without additional technical requirements or a promise of inclusion.

support.locator: Valid indexing and serving rules > noindex, nosnippet, max-snippet
support.note: Meta directives and HTTP headers constrain indexing and preview use. Restrictive conflicts take precedence; nosnippet also restricts direct input to Google AI features.

tactics.title: Separate search crawling from training
tactics.problem: A single AI-bot policy can conflate independent choices.
implementation: Document OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot policies separately.
Check the deployed rules against current OpenAI documentation.
verification: A test matrix demonstrates each bot receives the intended policy.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Intentional search access removes a preventable discovery barrier.
tactics.anti_pattern: Describing GPTBot access as a requirement for ChatGPT search.
tactics.measurement: Report OAI-SearchBot policy drift separately from training-policy drift.

support.locator: Overview; OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot table rows
support.note: OpenAI distinguishes search and model-training crawlers and makes their robots policies independent. It recommends permitting searchbot plus published IP ranges for intended search access.

tactics.title: Check the CDN response as well as robots
tactics.problem: A permissive file does not bypass an edge challenge.
implementation: Probe canonical HTML through the public hostname.
Inspect trusted crawler logs and verify published IP ranges before changing narrow firewall rules.
verification: Priority HTML is accessible without a challenge under the intended verified-crawler policy.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Reducing false bot blocks may improve successful retrieval.
tactics.anti_pattern: Allowlisting a user-agent string as if it authenticated a crawler.
tactics.measurement: Measure verified search crawler challenge and 4xx rates by provider.

support.locator: OAI-SearchBot and published IP ranges
support.note: Supports provider-specific access; edge log review is our operational method.

support.locator: Technical requirements
support.note: Supports crawl access; an HTTP probe does not prove indexing.

tactics.title: Keep the answer in initial HTML
tactics.problem: Some clients cannot recover essential content from a client-only shell.
implementation: Fetch a representative article without executing JavaScript.
Render the main answer, source links, and page identity in initial HTML.
Treat initial HTML as a reliability choice for the intended clients; Google can render JavaScript, so compare initial and rendered output before diagnosing a blocker.
verification: A plain HTML extraction contains the answer and its qualifications.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: More clients may retrieve complete content on their first fetch.
tactics.anti_pattern: Claiming that Google cannot render JavaScript.
tactics.measurement: Compare required-answer extraction coverage with and without JavaScript.

support.locator: How Google processes JavaScript
support.note: Google renders JavaScript; initial HTML is our broader-client reliability choice.

tactics.title: Generate canonical sitemaps from the built output
tactics.problem: Repository files do not prove public discovery artifacts exist.
implementation: Generate sitemap entries from published canonical pages.
Fetch the deployed sitemap and sample its destinations.
verification: Entries resolve to intended canonical indexable pages; lastmod reflects content changes.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Accurate discovery hints may help crawlers find changed resources.
tactics.anti_pattern: Including drafts or updating all lastmod values on every build.
tactics.measurement: Track sitemap URL validity and discovered-to-indexed lag separately.

support.locator: Referenced URLs properties; Additional notes about XML sitemaps; How to create a sitemap
support.note: Sitemaps should contain preferred canonical absolute URLs. Accurate lastmod refers to significant page changes. Google permits CMS, database-driven, manual and automatic generation.

tactics.title: Notify participating engines after real changes
tactics.problem: Repeated unchanged notifications add noise without new content.
implementation: Create a changed canonical URL set from the release diff.
Submit it to IndexNow only after verifying the host key and live content.
verification: Retain request time, URL count, response, and a separate later indexing observation.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Timely change notification may shorten discovery delays on participating engines.
tactics.anti_pattern: Calling an accepted notification an indexed page or Google submission.
tactics.measurement: Measure change-to-notification time and independently observed recrawl lag.

support.locator: Submitting One URL; Submitting set of URLs; Verifying ownership via the key
support.note: IndexNow accepts added, updated and deleted URLs and checks host ownership through a key file. A successful response acknowledges receipt, not indexing.

tactics.title: Inspect representative URLs after publication
tactics.problem: Local validation cannot identify the selected indexed version.
implementation: Select a small cohort covering templates and known failures.
Use authorized URL Inspection evidence to record indexed and live states separately.
Record the indexed Google-selected canonical separately; a live test cannot predict canonical selection or guarantee search appearance.
verification: Each observation has URL, timestamp, inspection type, and evidence status.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: A bounded inspection cohort may reveal real eligibility blockers earlier.
tactics.anti_pattern: Inferring indexing from site: search or a successful deployment.
tactics.measurement: Track verified indexed coverage within the fixed cohort; leave uninspected URLs unknown.

support.locator: About the indexed URL status; Inspect a live URL
support.note: Indexed and live observations differ; a live pass does not establish indexed canonical selection.

tactics.title: Give each recurring intent a primary page
tactics.problem: Overlapping articles split maintenance and confuse navigation.
implementation: Group actual reader tasks from search and support evidence.
Assign an owner URL and distinguish any necessary supporting pages.
verification: The intent map names one primary answer and the unique job of each support page.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Concentrated maintenance may improve answer completeness.
tactics.anti_pattern: Creating one page for every keyword permutation.
tactics.measurement: Track query-to-landing-page fragmentation and qualified visits per intent.

support.locator: People-first content
support.note: Supports useful task coverage; one primary page per task is our maintenance convention.

support.locator: Reasons to specify a canonical URL
support.note: Duplicate consolidation does not require merging distinct tasks.

tactics.title: Build a task-based topic hub
tactics.problem: A chronological archive hides the next useful resource.
implementation: Choose a recurring task with multiple meaningful stages.
Link its prerequisites, main guide, worked example, and troubleshooting from a hub.
verification: Every link answers a named reader need and all destinations are live.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: A coherent path may improve discovery of deeper useful pages.
tactics.anti_pattern: A keyword cloud with no editorial explanation.
tactics.measurement: Measure hub-to-target clicks and orphan-page count.

support.locator: Internal links
support.note: Supports relevant crawlable links; a staged hub is our design proposal.

tactics.title: Use descriptive crawlable anchors
tactics.problem: Clickable scripts and generic labels obscure destinations.
implementation: Replace navigation-only event handlers with real href anchors.
Name the destination task in concise visible link text.
verification: An HTML link extractor finds priority destinations and meaningful labels.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Readable links support crawling and informed navigation.
tactics.anti_pattern: Stuffing all variants into anchor text.
tactics.measurement: Count priority links lacking usable href or descriptive accessible text.

support.locator: Make your links crawlable; Write good anchor text
support.note: Google recommends resolvable href anchors and contextual, concise, descriptive labels; script-only events are unreliable for extracting links. Keyword stuffing is discouraged.

tactics.title: Check discovery paths to important pages
tactics.problem: A sitemap alone can conceal pages absent from normal navigation.
implementation: Crawl links from public entry pages.
Join the discovered set with the canonical publication inventory.
verification: Each priority page has a relevant inbound internal link.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Removing orphan pages may improve both human and crawler discovery.
tactics.anti_pattern: Adding site-wide unrelated footer links solely to satisfy a counter.
tactics.measurement: Report priority orphans by template and their resolution dates.

support.locator: Internal links: cross-reference your own content
support.note: Important pages should receive at least one internal link. Contextual links to useful related resources are encouraged; no universal ideal link count is prescribed.

tactics.title: Align duplicate URL signals
tactics.problem: Tracking and slash variants can disagree about the primary address.
implementation: Choose the preferred URL for each duplicate group.
Align redirects, canonical links, sitemap entries, and internal references.
verification: All sampled signals identify the same target; external selected-canonical evidence stays separate.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: Consistent preferences may reduce duplicate processing.
tactics.anti_pattern: Canonicalizing genuinely different answers to one broad category.
tactics.measurement: Track conflicting canonical signals and later selected-canonical mismatches.

support.locator: Best practices
support.note: Google advises using consistent canonical preferences across methods and internal links, including self-referential canonical links. Inconsistent sitemap and canonical targets should be avoided.

tactics.title: Constrain unbounded filter combinations
tactics.problem: Facets can generate an effectively endless crawl space.
implementation: Inventory index-worthy filtered views and empty combinations.
Apply a deliberate crawl and URL policy to nonessential combinations.
verification: Tests cover useful filters, empty results, reordered parameters, and repeated values.
tactics.impact_hypothesis: A finite crawl surface may preserve resources for useful views.
tactics.anti_pattern: Blocking every filter without checking real demand and content value.
tactics.measurement: Compare unique crawler-requested facet URLs and useful indexed filter pages.

support.locator: Managing crawling; Prevent crawling; Ensure the faceted navigation URLs are optimal for the web
support.note: Facets can create costly URL spaces. Google separates useful indexable combinations from blocked unnecessary ones; stable filter ordering, no duplicates and404 for invalid/no-result combinations are recommended.

tactics.title: Make long collections reachable without scrolling
tactics.problem: Infinite scroll may hide records from simple clients.
implementation: Expose sequential anchor href links and distinct page URLs with appropriate page-specific canonicals.
